# ship bar

> A free, copy-paste method for making AI-built websites stop looking vibe-coded: art direction rules, a banned-pattern list, and a separate reviewer agent that scores each build out of 10 against a 9.7 ship bar. By Travis Curnutte.

## Key facts
- Cohort: 20 narrow-lens reviewers score independently; final score is the median; ship only at median 9.7+ with zero blockers.
- Self-test: this page was run through its own cohort. Round 1: median 9.20, 2 blockers. Round 2: median 9.70, 0 blockers. Round 3: median 9.70, 0 blockers.
- Reviewer agent scores from screenshots at 1440px desktop and 390px mobile, plus Lighthouse (performance, accessibility, best practices, SEO), console errors, horizontal-overflow checks and a computed-style scan for banned patterns.
- It returns a score plus ranked fixes, most important first, and never edits the repo.
- Banned: glows, gradients, glassmorphism, floating phones, bento grids, confetti, serif headlines, filler copy.
- Cohorts: several narrow-lens reviewer agents score independently; fixes are merged by rank.
- LeadLens example: one product went v6 "still felt a tad vibe coded" to v12 passing at 9.7 (accessibility 100); v13 dropped to 9.3 when a sticky CTA covered a form field and a gradient slipped in.
